article_title: A Dynamic Geometry-Centered Teacher Professional Development Program and Its Impact
citation: Zhonghong Jiang, Edwin Dickey, Alexander White, Ewelina McBroom, M. Alejandra Sorto, & Alana Rosenwasser. (2015). A Dynamic Geometry-Centered Teacher Professional Development Program and Its Impact. Proceedings of the 37th annual meeting of the North American Chapter of the International Group for the Psychology of Mathematics Education, East Lansing, MI: Michigan State University.
title: Eight-event DG investigation cycle: task, construction, initial conjecture, dragging/measuring experimentation, conjecture testing, iteration, summarizing reflection, and proof development
description: A reusable lesson-level pattern for dynamic geometry investigations, printed as the article's own enumerated list of PD activity events. Each activity moves teachers (and, by modeling, their students) from a presented task through construction in DG software to conjecturing, testing with "dragging, measuring, and multiple, linked representations", and finally developing explanations to prove or disprove conjectures.
requirements: Access to DG software (the project used Geometer's Sketchpad) so learners can construct objects and experiment by dragging and measuring
A facilitator who circulates, asks questions, and initiates whole-group discussions as needed
constraints: The pattern was implemented with high school geometry topics (triangle congruence and similarity, special quadrilaterals, circles, geometric transformations) and school-year follow-up aligned to district scope and sequence
target_learners: high school geometry teachers in professional development
high school geometry students (via modeled instruction)
target_learning_goals: conjecturing, conjecture testing, and proving abilities
examples: PD facilitators modeled what teachers were expected to do with their students; one observed teacher's students explored triangle midsegments, made and measured conjectures, and discussed observations while the teacher guided through questioning
